spans.claim: Mrs. Harlowe died a natural death on the night of April 27th
spans.anchor: Mrs. Harlowe died, so far as we know, quite peacefully in her bed during the night

spans.claim: Betty Harlowe was at a ball from 9pm to after 1am
spans.anchor: Mademoiselle was dancing with her friends on this night when she is supposed to be committing the most monstrous of crimes
spans.span: Yes, Mademoiselle was dancing with her friends on this night when she is supposed to be committing the most monstrous of crimes.

spans.claim: No trace of poison was found in Mrs. Harlowe's body
spans.anchor: no more morphia was discovered in it than one sleeping-dose would explain and no trace at all of any other poison
spans.span: that no more morphia was discovered in it than one sleeping-dose would explain and no trace at all of any other poison?

spans.claim: The poison arrow head was found disguised as a pen-holder
spans.anchor: There it was--the slender, pencil-like shaft expanding into a slight bulb where the fingers held it, and the nib inserted into the tiny cleft made for the stem of the iron dart
spans.span: There it was--the slender, pencil-like shaft expanding into a slight bulb where the fingers held it, and the nib inserted into the tiny cleft made for the stem of the iron dart!

spans.claim: Betty Harlowe and Francine Rollard administered the poison
spans.anchor: Betty Harlowe stretched out upon the bed to represent Madame, and Francine whispering 'That will do now'
spans.span: Betty Harlowe stretched out upon the bed to represent Madame, and Francine whispering 'That will do now'?

spans.claim: Ann Upcott was abducted to prevent her revealing the truth
spans.anchor: Ann Upcott was bound hand and foot and brought here

spans.claim: Jean Cladel was murdered to silence him
spans.anchor: Jean Cladel has been murdered--cruelly

spans.claim: The secret passage connects Maison Grenelle and Hôtel de Brebizart
spans.anchor: a secret passage in that age of secret passages
spans.span: Between this house and the Maison Grenelle he had constructed a secret passage in that age of secret passages.

spans.claim: The clock on the marquetry cabinet was moved to mislead
spans.anchor: the clock was not upon the mantelshelf but upon the marquetry cabinet
spans.span: When the seals were removed and we entered this room for the first time, the clock was not upon the mantelshelf but upon the marquetry cabinet.

spans.claim: The pearl necklace was stolen to provide motive
spans.anchor: A pearl necklace ... had disappeared

spans.claim: Boris Waberski's accusation was a false lead
spans.anchor: Boris Waberski ... declared that Betty Harlowe did wilfully give to her adoptive mother an overdose of a narcotic

spans.claim: Anonymous letters were typed on a Corona machine
spans.anchor: the letters were typed upon a Corona machine
spans.span: do not tell me that you have discovered that the letters were typed upon a Corona machine.

spans.claim: Hanaud replaced the Treatise on Strophanthus on the bookshelf
spans.anchor: I replace the book about the arrows on the bookshelf in its obvious place
spans.span: I replace the book about the arrows on the bookshelf in its obvious place.

spans.claim: Betty Harlowe sent a telegram to London about Hanaud's involvement
spans.anchor: The telegram sent to my firm by Miss Harlowe on Monday
spans.span: The telegram sent to my firm by Miss Harlowe on Monday--yes, by George, this last Monday.

spans.claim: Ann Upcott's story of the night is partly true but adapted
spans.anchor: Ann Upcott is left alone after Mademoiselle Harlowe's departure to Monsieur de Pouillac's Ball
spans.span: Ann Upcott is left alone after Mademoiselle Harlowe's departure to Monsieur de Pouillac's Ball.

spans.claim: The poison arrow was used as a hypodermic needle
spans.anchor: the head of the arrow-shaft should be the pen-holder with which I have written this memorandum
spans.span: For Life, the incorrigible Dramatist, had arranged that the head of the arrow-shaft should be the pen-holder with which I have written this memorandum.

spans.claim: The secret passage was used to move between houses
spans.anchor: the secret passage was lost ... Simon Harlowe ... restored the passage

spans.claim: The murder was committed at half-past ten
spans.anchor: the hour was half-past ten

spans.claim: The missing pearl necklace was found hidden in a matchbox
spans.anchor: a string of pearls perfectly graded in size
spans.span: From the cotton-wool he took a string of pearls perfectly graded in size, and gleaming softly with a pink lustre which, even to his untutored eyes, was indescribably lovely.

spans.claim: Jean Cladel was admitted by a friend and murdered
spans.anchor: He was admitted as a friend or a client
spans.span: I think that he was admitted as a friend or a client--I fancy Jean Cladel had not a few clients who preferred to call upon him by the back way in the dark of the night.

spans.claim: Betty Harlowe was the mastermind behind the murder and blackmail
spans.anchor: Betty Harlowe had prepared to divert suspicion from herself upon Ann Upcott
spans.span: Betty Harlowe had prepared to divert suspicion from herself upon Ann Upcott, should suspicion arise.

spans.claim: The facade of Notre Dame symbolizes Ann Upcott's guilt
spans.anchor: That, Monsieur Frobisher, is what I sent you out to see
spans.span: That, Monsieur Frobisher, is what I sent you out to see," said Hanaud gravely.
